name: Redirect settings
subtitle: What gets recorded when a visitor hits a missing page, and what this plugin offers you when it finds one. None of this changes rules you have already written.

elements.label: Record paths that lead nowhere
elements.hint: Every address a visitor asks for that has no page is written to Broken Links, once per address with a running count. Leave this on while you are migrating a site — it is the list that tells you which old links people still follow. Turn it off once the list has gone quiet. Your redirects keep working either way; this only controls whether misses are written down.

elements.label: Suggest where a broken link should go
elements.hint: When you open a broken link, the plugin compares it against every page, product, post and collection you have and offers the closest matches. Most broken links are near misses — a slug that was tidied up, a word that changed — so the page you want is usually already on the list.

elements.label: How similar a suggestion has to be
elements.hint: 100 means only a near-identical address is offered; 0 means anything is. 70 is a good starting point. Below about 60 you will get suggestions that share a few letters and nothing else, and reading past them costs more time than they save. If a broken link you expected to be recognised is not being offered anything, lower this by ten and look again.

elements.label: Forget dealt-with entries after
elements.hint: Used only by the Prune history button on the Broken Links screen — nothing is ever deleted on a timer, because this plugin cannot run background jobs. Entries you have not dealt with are never removed at any age: an old broken link is still a broken link. Leave this empty and Prune will tell you there is nothing to do.

elements.label: Show suggestions to visitors on your 404 page
elements.hint: Offers the same near-matches to the visitor who hit the dead link, so they can carry on instead of leaving. This only appears if your theme makes room for it: a theme has to include the plugin's not-found slot, and one that does not will show nothing at all with no error. Switch it on, visit a made-up address on your shop, and look — if nothing appears, your theme has not made room and your theme developer needs to add it.

elements.label: Addresses never worth recording
elements.hint: One pattern per row. Use * to stand for anything: .git/* catches everything under .git, *.sql catches every address ending in .sql, and .env catches exactly that. Without a few of these, Broken Links fills up with automated scanners probing for files and software your site does not serve, and the handful of real broken links your visitors actually hit gets buried. Matching ignores upper and lower case.
